question: In tuberculous meningitis, the CSF glucose level is characteristically normal, which helps distinguish TBM from acute bacterial meningitis.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. CSF glucose in TBM is characteristically very low — both bacterial meningitis and TBM show markedly reduced glucose. It is viral meningitis that typically has normal CSF glucose. TBM is distinguished by lymphocytic pleocytosis, very high protein, and the characteristic cobweb clot on standing.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is false. In TBM, CSF glucose is characteristically very low (often <50% of blood glucose), similar to bacterial meningitis. TBM is distinguished from bacterial meningitis by its lymphocytic (not neutrophilic) predominance, very high protein, and the pathognomonic cobweb coagulum on standing.
